content: Ben Humble resided in Arrochar from 1960 to 1970. He was a highly productive author and a distinguished Scottish climber who played a pivotal role in establishing the modern Scottish Mountain Rescue teams as we know them today. In addition to his mountaineering achievements, he was an enthusiastic photographer and filmmaker. Ben Humble was born in Dumbarton in 1903, one of the sons of the manager of Dennystown Forge. Despite being completely deaf, he pursued a career in dentistry and later made significant contributions to the field of forensic dentistry. His deafness, however, contributed to his somewhat gruff demeanor, earning him the nickname Bennie. A particular incident involving an unflattering published photograph, known as the Humble Kipper, which depicted him during breakfast, led to a decade-long estrangement from the photographer responsible for the image. For more comprehensive information, you can refer to the definitive web biography of Ben Humble available on the Arrochar, Tarbet, and Ardlui Heritage Group website. Ben Humble passed away in 1977.
